critical_code_review_comments: workflows.py send_email: `_assert_safe_email` rejects any body containing 'http://' — legitimate transactional emails may include http links (e.g. tracking domains behind proxies) and will silently fail with 'Email content not allowed'. Consider allow-listing per-tenant safe hosts, or restrict only user-templated content, not app-generated wrappers.

workflows.py run_workflow email step uses payload.get('email') as recipient. For chat_lead the sample has email='' so email actions are silently dropped with status='queued reason=no recipient' — that's OK, but the UI shows this as a success glyph because status starts with a 'q' (queued not in the success list). Consider surfacing 'skipped: no recipient' distinctly.

workflows.py tpl() naive string replace is not HTML-escaped when it lands in the email HTML wrapper (escape() is called on final body, so OK); but `subject` uses tpl(...) too and is passed straight into subject[:200] without escape — subject in email header is fine, but reflect this in UI display.

DeployHub.publish() calls `/preview/toggle` when preview_token exists and `/preview/regenerate` when not — the regenerate path also creates a token but doesn't set preview_enabled explicitly; verify that regenerate turns it live in one call (Nexus works because token existed).

workflows.fire_event iterates all matching workflows sequentially in the request path of /public/contact — if a webhook action is slow (10s timeout each), the public contact submission can block up to ~50s. Move fire_event into asyncio.create_task for non-test dispatch.

WorkflowsPanel.jsx: no server-side validation of condition op values from client; op 'contains' etc. are validated by backend OPS map, but arbitrary strings for 'field' allow evaluating on any payload key — low risk, but consider gating fields to samples[trigger] keys in UI.
DeployHub row grid uses fixed 5-column layout; on narrow desktop (<1200px) columns overlap. Not tested at tablet width.
